logline: A timid Mumbai constable goes undercover as a sex worker to infiltrate a drug cartel - and the assignment cracks open a side of herself she was never supposed to find.

renewal.note: Season 2 released June 17, 2022, concluding the series. No renewal announced; the story reached a natural end with Bhumi's arc resolved.

bollymeter.basis: Season 1 holds 20% on Rotten Tomatoes from 5 critics and a 38% audience score. Critics largely found Imtiaz Ali's male-gaze framing undermining an otherwise bold premise; Aaditi Pohankar's performance was the near-universal saving grace.

She is too focused on the seasoning, not the meat. It throws only sporadic light on the one strong female character.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 arrived on Netflix India in March 2020 to a divisive critical reception, landing at 20 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 5 reviews. The premise - a repressed constable discovering her own agency through an undercover operation - had genuine potential, and Aaditi Pohankar's interior performance gave critics something to hold onto. The problem, as multiple reviewers identified, was the framing: Imtiaz Ali and Divya Johry's writing kept the camera at the service of the male gaze, turning a story ostensibly about female awakening into something critics called sleazy and evasive. NDTV found it never crackles; Hindustan Times called it sleazy and sloppy. Vijay Varma's menacing Sasya was noted as the season's best-drawn figure - a pointed commentary on where the creative energy actually went.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes Bhumika's claustrophobic home life and her recruitment into the anti-narcotics operation. The setup is efficient and Pohankar's underconfident physicality is instantly compelling - the episode earns attention before the series wastes it.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bhumika's first interaction with the cartel boss Nayak - the discomfort is palpable and the threat register is immediately different from anything in the police station scenes.

critic_note.text: At the heart of this brisk series is a thoroughly dark, twisted relationship between a conscience-less mobster and an unwilling undercover cop.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 registers 33% on Rotten Tomatoes from 3 critics. Reviewers noted continued evolution in Pohankar's performance but flagged drag pacing and poor writing from Akhil Arora (Gadgets360), calling it a showcase of the creator's weaknesses.

pull_quotes.text: The second season offers up a continued evolution in Bhumi's character.

seasons.review_body: Season 2, released June 2022, carried forward the series' core problem: a character whose inner transformation Pohankar played with real conviction, trapped in writing that critics found repetitive and poorly structured. Rotten Tomatoes logged only 3 reviews for a 33 percent score, itself a signal of how little critical attention the second season generated. Decider credited Bhumi's continued evolution; Film Companion praised a compelling vulgarity in the show's register; Gadgets360 called it a glorious showcase of the creator's weaknesses, with scenes that drag. The series concluded here, ending a run that promised more than it delivered but gave Pohankar a showcase role that launched her to wider attention.
seasons.season_over_season: Pohankar's performance deepens but the writing regresses - Season 2 is slower and more repetitive than the already-flawed first run.
